newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Gulf crude business steadies in modest action.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Gulf crude business steadies in modest action.

text.p: Gasoline prices surged again on the NYMEX futures market Friday and lifted U.S. outright cash crudes in the process, but a modestly traded grade sector offered little motivation for securing domestic barrels.

Benchmark September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing talked late around 15 cents firmer at $20.20-30 a barrel. September/October WTI/Cushing spreads narrowed to the end, talked at -2 cents from spreads closer to -10 cents earlier.
Gasoline buying started after news of European refinery troubles hit the market, leaving traders concerned about supplies meant for the New York Harbor in the coming weeks.

The BP/Texaco Nerefco joint venture in Rotterdam experienced a snafu, forcing the shutdown of the plant's 55,000 barrel per day (bpd) catalytic cracker. Further, the BP/Mobil 60,0000 bpd Coryton cat cracker in the U.K. was shut for technical reasons.
There was no word from the United Nations to unsettle traders, though moves by U.S. trader Bayoil to provisionally secure tonnage for shipping Iraqi crude was noted.

Most believe the U.N. will come forward with approval for Baghdad's aid distribution plan at the start of next week, and shortly thereafter, Iraq will submit a pricing mechanism for governing oil sales contracts.

None of the news in market could rustle excitement for Gulf traders looking to move domestic grade barrels. Existing fundamentals and morbid arbitrage for North Sea Brent created static trading conditions.
Many traders were absent from offices, taking part in a Houston-area golf tournament sponsored by Amoco.
Late talk had Midland/WTI at a 30-28 discount to the September benchmark, and Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James holding a 23-25 cents premium, after selling at +24 cents.
Sour grades floated around a $1.45 discount, with Eugene Island also steady at $1.35-30 under cash WTI/Cushing.
September WTI/Cushing Postings Plus moved at $1.98 and later at $2.00, in conjunction with shrinking September/October rolls, traders said.
